disease_label_per_paper: Varicella-zoster virus hemorrhagic encephalitis with vasculopathy mimicking toxoplasmosis relapse
presentation_summary: 37-year-old woman with HIV-1 infection and cerebral toxoplasmosis diagnosed four months earlier presented with seizures, confusion, and fever after weeks of apathy and self-neglect.
She had poor adherence to antitoxoplasmosis and antiretroviral drugs after prior improvement.
At admission she had slow verbal and motor responses, disorientation, pyrexia 38 C, severe anemia, CD4 count 4 cells/uL, and HIV viral load 114,294 copies/mL.
Brain MRI initially showed increased number and contrast uptake of lesions, so toxoplasmosis treatment and ART were restarted with some radiologic response.

Two weeks later she worsened with fluctuating consciousness, apathy, aphasia, and food and medication refusal; MRI showed more T2/FLAIR lesions and multiple new hemorrhagic and enhancing vascular-territory lesions.
CSF showed 8 WBC/mm3, protein 1330 mg/dL, and VZV DNA positivity with negative cryptococcal antigen, HIV, CMV, EBV, HSV, adenovirus PCR, and antineuronal antibodies.
Despite acyclovir, she deteriorated to no eye or verbal response, food and medication refusal, and tetraparesis with hyperreflexia and bilateral extensor plantar responses.
Repeat CSF showed 1350 erythrocytes/mm3, protein 2400 mg/dL, no lymphocytes, and lower VZV DNA copies; EEG excluded status epilepticus.
VZV hemorrhagic encephalitis with vasculopathy was assumed, and foscarnet plus IV methylprednisolone were added, with rapid clinical improvement despite persistent widespread MRI lesions.

quality_warnings: This case includes a major mimic context: prior toxoplasmosis lesions and advanced HIV. Those facts are retained rather than removed.
VZV PCR and vasculopathic MRI pattern are rankable here because the paper's final entity is VZV hemorrhagic encephalitis with vasculopathy, not isolated stroke without encephalitis.
Day-14 and later events are structured in clinical_course_events because the VZV diagnosis emerged after deterioration from the initial toxoplasmosis-relapse framing.
